examples.text: Philosophy, unlike most other subjects, does not try to extend our knowledge by discovering new information about the world. Instead it tries to deepen our understanding through rumination on what is already closest to us — the experiences, thoughts, concepts, and activities that make up our lives but that ordinarily escape our notice precisely because they are so familiar. Philosophy begins by finding utterly mysterious the things that are most prosaic.

Philosophy begins by finding (ii) ________ the things that are (iii) ________.

families.title: Abundance and rapid growth
families.scene: বিরিয়ানির হাঁড়িতে এত ডিম বাড়ছে যে মুরগিরা বেকারভাতার লাইনে দাঁড়াল!
families.distinctions: Abound means exist in large numbers; proliferate and burgeon mean grow rapidly; fecund and fruitful concern productivity.

families.title: Increase or expand
families.scene: অহংকারী বেলুনটা পদোন্নতি পেতে ফুলতে ফুলতে সিলিংয়ে আটকাল!
families.distinctions: Augment adds; escalate intensifies; distend swells; aggrandize increases power or status.

families.title: Spread widely
families.scene: একটা গুজব ছাড়তেই পাড়ার কাকিমারা বিনা বেতনে সম্প্রচার শুরু করলেন!
families.distinctions: Disseminate and propagate spread information; diffuse and disperse spread or scatter more broadly.

families.title: Everywhere or widespread
families.scene: মশা সবখানে হাজির—মনে হয় বাড়ির প্রতিটি কোণে তার শাখা অফিস!
families.distinctions: Rampant usually describes something harmful spreading without restraint.

families.title: Decrease or weaken
families.scene: বেতন আসার পর মানিব্যাগের টাকা কমতে কমতে শেষে শুধু বাসের টিকিট!
families.distinctions: Curtail deliberately cuts something short; the others describe reduction or weakening.

families.title: Relieve or moderate
families.scene: পরীক্ষার ফল দেখে মাথাব্যথা; মা চা দিতেই দুশ্চিন্তার ভলিউম একটু কমল!
families.distinctions: Ameliorate improves a bad situation; assuage soothes a feeling; extenuating lessens seriousness or blame.

families.title: Calm or appease
families.scene: রাগী স্যারকে রসগোল্লা দিতেই বজ্রপাত বন্ধ—এখন মিষ্টি মিষ্টি কথা!
families.distinctions: Conciliatory describes an intention to restore goodwill; appease can also mean satisfy a demand.

families.title: Peaceful or emotionally steady
families.scene: চারদিকে বিয়ে-বাড়ির ডিজে, কিন্তু বিড়ালটা যোগগুরুর মতো শান্ত!
families.distinctions: Equanimity is a balanced state of mind; phlegmatic suggests a calm temperament.

families.title: Unemotional
families.scene: ফোন নর্দমায় পড়ল, তবু মুখে ভাব নেই—রোবটও বলল, দাদা একটু কাঁদুন!
families.distinctions: Stoic stresses endurance; stolid stresses little visible emotion.

families.title: Quiet or inactive
families.scene: অফিসের প্রিন্টার এত দিন নিষ্ক্রিয় যে তার ওপর আলুর চাষ শুরু হয়েছে!
families.distinctions: Fallow also describes uncultivated land; abeyance is temporary suspension.

families.title: Short-lived
families.scene: ফুচকার সামনে ডায়েটের প্রতিজ্ঞা—জীবনকাল মাত্র তিন সেকেন্ড!
families.distinctions: Evanescent especially suggests quickly fading away.

families.title: Lasting or unchanging
families.scene: দাদুর রেডিও বদলায়নি, অভ্যাসও বদলায়নি—এখন রেডিওটাই পারিবারিক শাসক!
families.distinctions: Perennial means recurring or lasting; incessant means continuous; perpetuate and ossify are verbs.

families.title: Old-fashioned
families.scene: ভিডিয়ো কলে দাদু কবুতর পাঠালেন; বললেন, আমার পুরোনো পদ্ধতিই সেরা!
families.distinctions: Anachronistic belongs to the wrong time; obsolete is no longer useful; dowdy concerns style.

families.title: New or developing
families.scene: নতুন স্টার্টআপের নাম আছে, চেয়ার নেই—বস এখনও মেঝেতে জন্ম নিচ্ছেন!
families.distinctions: Fledgling can describe a beginner; inchoate means not fully formed.

families.title: Clear or understandable
families.scene: ব্যাখ্যা এত পরিষ্কার যে ঘুমন্ত বিড়ালও উঠে বলল, এবার বুঝেছি!
families.distinctions: Explicable means capable of explanation; limpid and pellucid can also describe clear water.

families.title: Explain or make clear
families.scene: ম্যাগির জট ছাড়িয়ে স্যার বোঝালেন—এটা নুডলস, মেট্রোর মানচিত্র নয়!
families.distinctions: Decipher works out a difficult meaning; delineate describes precisely.

families.title: Obscure or difficult to understand
families.scene: অঙ্কের বই খুলতেই মনে হলো এলিয়েন তার বিয়ের বাজেট লিখেছে!
families.distinctions: Enigmatic and inscrutable suggest mystery; opaque and obscure can have additional literal senses.

families.title: Confuse or puzzle
families.scene: বিয়ের বাফেতে ডায়েটের নিয়ম বুঝতে গিয়ে পুষ্টিবিদই তালগোল পাকালেন!
families.distinctions: Obfuscate makes something unclear; the other adjectives describe the confused person.

families.title: Complicated
families.scene: এমন প্যাঁচানো ফর্ম যে নাম লিখতে গিয়ে জন্মতারিখেরও অবসর হয়ে গেল!
families.distinctions: Tortuous also means physically twisting.

families.title: Indistinct or formless
families.scene: পুডিংটা এত আকারহীন আর ঘোলা যে আয়নাও তাকে চিনতে অস্বীকার করল!
families.distinctions: Amorphous lacks form; turbid is cloudy or confused.

families.title: Undeniable or decisive
families.scene: হাঁড়ি খালি, মুখে ভাত—বিড়ালের অপরাধ আর অস্বীকার করার উপায় নেই!
families.distinctions: Axiomatic is self-evident; conclusive settles a question with evidence.

families.title: Persuasive or credible
families.scene: যুক্তি এত জোরালো যে ঝগড়াটে টিয়াও বলল, ঠিক আছে, আপনি জিতলেন!
families.distinctions: Sound and tenable concern validity or defensibility; rational concerns reason.

families.title: Real or genuine
families.scene: রসগোল্লাটা সত্যিই আছে—ছুঁয়ে দেখতেই দোকানদার বলল, এবার দাম দিন!
families.distinctions: Tangible and palpable stress perceptibility. The PDF gives palpable an apparently incorrect definition; see the source note.

families.title: False or misleading
families.scene: অনলাইনের রাজপ্রাসাদ খুলে দেখা গেল জুতোর বাক্স—ছবির রাজত্ব ভুয়া!
families.distinctions: Specious and sophistry stress misleading plausibility; delusion is a false belief.

families.title: Lie or conceal the truth
families.scene: হোমওয়ার্ক খেয়েছে ডাইনোসর—মিথ্যা বানাতে বানাতে ছাত্র জুরাসিক পার্ক খুলল!
families.distinctions: Feign means pretend; fabricate invents; mendacity is dishonesty.

families.title: Mislead or deceive
families.scene: ধূর্ত শিয়াল অনলাইনে চাঁদের জমি বেচে ছাগলকে মহাকাশের জমিদার বানাল!
families.distinctions: Beguile can also charm; swindle concerns fraudulent gain; feint is a deceptive maneuver.

families.title: Evade or avoid an issue
families.scene: বাসন মাজার কথা উঠতেই ভাই আন্তর্জাতিক জলবায়ু সম্মেলনে চলে গেল!
families.distinctions: Equivocate uses ambiguous language; shirk avoids a duty.

families.title: Hide or keep secret
families.scene: শেষ লাড্ডুটা আলমারিতে লুকিয়েছি; গোয়েন্দা পিঁপড়েরা গোপন অভিযান চালাচ্ছে!
families.distinctions: Ulterior usually concerns a concealed motive; furtive suggests stealth.

families.title: Reveal or make public
families.scene: চোরের গোঁফে দই—গোপন ভোজের খবর মুখই প্রকাশ করে দিল!
families.distinctions: Betray can mean reveal unintentionally; overt and patent describe openness or obviousness.

families.title: Noticeable or striking
families.scene: কালো জামায় এক বালতি সাদা দই—নজর এড়ানো তো দূর, চাঁদ থেকেও দেখা যায়!
families.distinctions: Flagrant concerns conspicuously bad behavior.

families.title: Truth or honesty
families.scene: সৎ ছাত্র বলল, উত্তর জানি না; পাশের বেঞ্চের টিয়াটা জানে!
families.distinctions: Candid describes openness; veracity is truthfulness; veritable means genuine.

families.title: Moral integrity
families.scene: সৎ দোকানদার বেশি টাকা ফেরত দিলেন; ক্যালকুলেটরও সম্মানে দাঁড়াল!
families.distinctions: Scrupulous can also mean extremely careful.

families.title: Corrupt or immoral
families.scene: ঘুষখোর দরজা খুলতে পাসওয়ার্ড চায় না—মিষ্টির বাক্সের নিচে খাম চায়!
families.distinctions: Venal specifically means open to bribery; reprobate and miscreant describe people.

families.title: Harmful
families.scene: পচা চাটনি খেয়ে পেট এমন প্রতিবাদ করল যে ভেতরেই মিছিল শুরু!
families.distinctions: Inimical and adverse can mean opposed; malign can also be a verb meaning speak ill of.

families.title: Harmless or helpful
families.scene: নিরীহ লাউ আর স্বাস্থ্যকর স্যুপ—পেট বলল, আজ অন্তত সংসদ শান্ত!
families.distinctions: Benign and innocuous mean harmless; salubrious and salutary mean beneficial. These are neighboring meanings.

families.title: Kind or generous
families.scene: কাকু এত উদার যে একটি বিস্কুট চাইতেই পুরো বিস্কুট কারখানা লিখে দিলেন!
families.distinctions: Lavish can also describe extravagant abundance.

families.title: Greedy or acquisitive
families.scene: লোভী কাঠবিড়ালি বাদাম জমিয়ে নিজের গাছেই জায়গা পেল না!
families.distinctions: Covet is the verb meaning strongly desire.

families.title: Driven by personal gain
families.scene: বন্ধু সাহায্য করার আগে বিল পাঠাল—বন্ধুত্বও নাকি ঘণ্টাপিছু ভাড়া!
families.distinctions: Mercenary stresses money; exploitative stresses unfair use of others.

families.title: Wasteful or extravagant
families.scene: বেতন পেয়েই সোনার চামচ কিনলাম; এখন সেই চামচে ধার করা ডাল খাই!
families.distinctions: Squander is a verb; exorbitant means unreasonably excessive, especially in price.

families.title: Frugal or stingy
families.scene: কৃপণ কাকু চা-পাতা শুকিয়ে আবার ব্যবহার করেন—চা-পাতাই পেনশন চাইছে!
families.distinctions: Economy can be positive efficiency; stint means supply too little; penurious can also mean very poor.

families.title: Plain or austere
families.scene: এমন বিলাসহীন ঘর যে বালিশও নিজের নরম স্বভাব লুকিয়ে কাঠ হয়ে আছে!
families.distinctions: Austere also describes a stern person; ascetic can name a person practicing self-denial.

families.title: Strict or harsh
families.scene: কড়া স্যারের ক্লাসে ঘড়িও দেরি করলে দাঁড়িয়ে কান ধরে!
families.distinctions: Exacting demands high standards; rigor is strictness or thoroughness.

families.title: Detailed or meticulous
families.scene: বিয়ের লুচির ব্যাস মেপে খাচ্ছেন—খুঁটিনাটিতে এমন যত্ন যে ফিতেও ক্লান্ত!
families.distinctions: Pedantic is often excessive attention to minor details; punctilious often concerns manners.

families.title: Hard to please
families.scene: খুঁতখুঁতে অতিথি বললেন, জিলিপির বাঁকটা বাঁ দিকে কেন, ডান দিকে নয়?
families.distinctions: Captious means inclined to find petty faults.

families.title: Thorough or comprehensive
families.scene: এত পূর্ণাঙ্গ তালিকা যে বাজারের ব্যাগে আলুর পারিবারিক ইতিহাসও ঢুকেছে!
families.distinctions: Encyclopedic stresses breadth of knowledge or coverage.

families.title: Careless or superficial
families.scene: দায়সারা ঝাড়ু দিয়ে ময়লা কার্পেটের নিচে পাঠালাম—ধুলো এখন ভাড়াটে!
families.distinctions: Perfunctory suggests routine effort; superficial concerns lack of depth; slovenly also concerns untidiness.

families.title: Indifferent or unconcerned
families.scene: বাড়ি জলে ভাসছে, সে নির্বিকার—বলছে, দেখো বিনা খরচে সুইমিং পুল!
families.distinctions: Complacent is self-satisfied; oblivious is unaware; the others concern lack of concern.

families.title: Tired or lacking energy
families.scene: এত ক্লান্ত যে সোফা থেকে ওঠার জন্য সোফাকেই অনুরোধপত্র পাঠাল!
families.distinctions: Enervate and debilitating describe weakening; languish is the verb for growing weak.

families.title: Lazy or ineffective
families.scene: অলস ভাই রিমোট তুলতে রোবট বানাল; এখন রোবটও অলস হয়ে শুয়ে আছে!
families.distinctions: Indolent means habitually lazy; feckless means ineffective or irresponsible.

families.title: Sleep-inducing or sleepy
families.scene: স্যারের বক্তৃতা শুনে অ্যালার্ম ঘড়িও নাক ডেকে ঘুমোল!
families.distinctions: Soporific induces sleep; somnolent describes drowsiness.

families.title: Slow or delaying
families.scene: কচ্ছপের অফিসে ফাইল এমন ধীরে চলে যে শামুক এসে তাড়া দিল!
families.distinctions: Ponderous can also mean heavy or very dull.

families.title: Energetic or lively
families.scene: বাচ্চার এত এনার্জি যে ইনভার্টার তাকে দেখে চার্জ হতে চাইছে!
families.distinctions: Frenetic suggests frantic activity; buoyant and jocund also suggest cheerfulness.

families.title: Enthusiastic or passionate
families.scene: বিনামূল্যে বিরিয়ানির খবর শুনে এমন উৎসাহ—বাসের আগেই সবাই গন্তব্যে!
families.distinctions: Alacrity means eager readiness to act.

families.title: Stimulate or energize
families.scene: চায়ের গন্ধে ঘুমন্ত অফিস জেগে উঠল—প্রমোশনের চেয়েও বড় অনুপ্রেরণা!
families.distinctions: Exhort urges; goad provokes; foment often encourages trouble; engender means bring about.

families.title: Exciting or captivating
families.scene: বাফের ঢাকনা উঠতেই এমন উত্তেজনা—পেট দাঁড়িয়ে হাততালি দিল!
families.distinctions: Heady suggests intoxication; tantalizing excites desire while withholding satisfaction.

families.title: Charm or fascinate
families.scene: জাদুকর এমন মুগ্ধ করলেন যে দর্শক টিকিটের দাম বাড়াতেও রাজি!
families.distinctions: Intrigue can also mean a secret scheme.

families.title: Enjoy or satisfy
families.scene: প্রিয় শেষ সন্দেশটা এত উপভোগ করলাম যে প্লেটও স্মৃতিচিহ্ন হয়ে গেল!
families.distinctions: Relish means enjoy; cherish means treasure; gratify means satisfy or please.

families.title: Happy or optimistic
families.scene: বিদ্যুৎ নেই, তবু আশাবাদী কাকু বললেন, মোমবাতির সেলফি আরও সুন্দর!
families.distinctions: Sanguine stresses optimism, especially despite difficulty.

families.title: Sad or gloomy
families.scene: শেষ রসগোল্লা পড়ে গেছে—মুখ এমন বিষণ্ন যেন মিষ্টির রাজা পদত্যাগ করেছেন!
families.distinctions: Crestfallen means disappointed; abject stresses an extreme or miserable condition.

families.title: Sorrow or emotional pain
families.scene: হারানো টিফিনের শোকে এমন গান ধরল যে পেঁয়াজও কাঁদতে বসল!
families.distinctions: Lament and dirge express grief; poignant evokes strong feeling; bereft means lacking or deprived.

families.title: Anxious or upset
families.scene: পরীক্ষার আগে পেটের প্রজাপতিরা দল বেঁধে বিমানবন্দর খুলেছে!
families.distinctions: Qualm is doubt or unease; aghast is shock or horror; fraught describes a tense situation.

families.title: Angry or irritated
families.scene: চায়ে চিনি কম—খিটখিটে কাকু এমন রাগলেন যে চামচ ক্ষমা চাইল!
families.distinctions: Indignant concerns perceived injustice; umbrage is offense; chagrin mixes embarrassment and frustration.

families.title: Irritating
families.scene: মশাটা কানের পাশে সারাক্ষণ বলে, আমার গানটা একটু শুনুন না!
families.distinctions: Both describe something annoying.

families.title: Hostility or hatred
families.scene: করলার প্রতি এমন ঘৃণা যে সবজির দোকান দেখলেই উল্টো বাসে ওঠে!
families.distinctions: Abhor and loathe are verbs; aversion is a strong dislike.

families.title: Disdain or contempt
families.scene: ভুয়া কবির কবিতা শুনে বিড়াল নাক সিটকে বলল, মিয়াঁও-ও এর চেয়ে ভালো!
families.distinctions: Disdain normally means contempt; the PDF's definition appears incorrect.

families.title: Aggressive or argumentative
families.scene: ঝগড়াটে মোরগ আয়নায় নিজেকেই দেখে বলল, বাইরে আয়, লড়বি?
families.distinctions: Fractious can mean unruly or irritable.

families.title: Conflict or upheaval
families.scene: বিয়েতে মাছের মাথা নিয়ে এমন ঝামেলা—বরও সালিশ কমিটিতে ঢুকে গেল!
families.distinctions: Contretemps is a minor mishap or disagreement; imbroglio is a complicated mess.

families.title: Provoke or attack
families.scene: শান্ত আড্ডায় কেউ বলল, আমার দলই সেরা—চায়ের কাপও যুদ্ধের হেলমেট পরল!
families.distinctions: Polemical describes controversial argument; incendiary incites conflict.

families.title: Scold or criticize harshly
families.scene: কাঁচা ভাত রাঁধায় এমন বকুনি খেলাম যে প্রেসার কুকারও আমার হয়ে কাঁদল!
families.distinctions: Admonish can also mean give urgent advice; decry and denounce are often public.

families.title: Biting or sharply critical
families.scene: সমালোচনা এত ধারালো যে লেখকের পেন্সিল নিজেই শান নিতে গেল!
families.distinctions: Trenchant can be incisive rather than hostile.

families.title: Long angry speech
families.scene: দীর্ঘ বকুনি চলছেই—মোবাইলের ব্যাটারি শেষ, বক্তার রাগের ব্যাটারি ফুল!
families.distinctions: These suggest extended verbal criticism or anger.

families.title: Mock or ridicule
families.scene: কবির গোঁফ এঁকে ব্যঙ্গচিত্র করতেই গোঁফটা মূল মানুষটির চেয়েও বিখ্যাত!
families.distinctions: Caricature exaggerates features; satirical describes criticism through humor or irony.

families.title: Slander or public disgrace
families.scene: গুজব ছড়াল বিড়াল ব্যাংক লুটেছে; বিড়াল বলল, আমার নামে এত অপবাদ কেন?
families.distinctions: Calumny and slander concern false damaging statements; stigmatize labels disgracefully; opprobrium is public condemnation.

families.title: Insult or disrespect
families.scene: বেয়াদব টিয়া স্যারকে বলল, আগে আপনি হোমওয়ার্ক দেখান!
families.distinctions: Impertinent can also mean irrelevant; irreverent can be humorous rather than insulting.

families.title: Rude or unrefined
families.scene: অভদ্র অতিথি সভার মাঝে চটি খুলে পাখা করলেন—শিষ্টাচার জানালা দিয়ে পালাল!
families.distinctions: Unseemly and indecorous describe inappropriate conduct more generally.

families.title: Polite or socially refined
families.scene: ভদ্র ছাগলও ফুলগাছ খাওয়ার আগে বলল, অনুমতি দিলে একটু চিবোই?
families.distinctions: Deportment means behavior or bearing; tact is skill in avoiding offense.

families.title: Friendly or sociable
families.scene: মিশুক কাকু বাসে উঠেই এমন আড্ডা দিলেন যে বাসটাই আত্মীয় হয়ে গেল!
families.distinctions: Comity is courteous harmony; convivial stresses enjoyment of company or festivities.

families.title: Reconcile or restore peace
families.scene: দুই বিড়ালের ঝগড়া মেটাতে দুধ ভাগ হলো; এখন তারা শান্তিচুক্তি চাটছে!
families.distinctions: Mediate intervenes between parties; detente is easing of tensions.

families.title: Agree or obey
families.scene: মা বললেন পড়তে বসো; ভাই এমন মেনে নিল যে বইও অবাক!
families.distinctions: Amenable means receptive; tractable means manageable, not necessarily obedient.

families.title: Submissive or flattering
families.scene: বস হাঁচতেই তোষামোদকারী বলল, স্যার, কী অসাধারণ সাংস্কৃতিক উপস্থাপনা!
families.distinctions: Fawn uses excessive flattery; grovel stresses humiliating submission.

families.title: Flatter or coax
families.scene: বোন মিষ্টি কথা বলে আমার শেষ চিপস নিল—চিপস গেল, প্রশংসা রয়ে গেল!
families.distinctions: Inveigle can suggest deception.

families.title: Beg or plead
families.scene: শেষ মিষ্টির জন্য এমন মিনতি করল যে সন্দেশই বলল, আচ্ছা আমাকেই খাও!
families.distinctions: Both involve earnest or humble requests.

families.title: Arrogant or domineering
families.scene: হুকুমবাজ রাজা নিজের ছাতাকেও বললেন, আমার সামনে এত মাথা তুলে কেন?
families.distinctions: Magisterial can neutrally mean authoritative; entitled suggests assuming special privileges.

families.title: Pretentious display
families.scene: দেখনদারি দাদার চপ্পলেও ঝাড়বাতি—পাড়ার বিদ্যুৎ দপ্তর চিন্তায়!
families.distinctions: Florid and baroque concern ornament; bombastic concerns inflated language; histrionic concerns exaggerated drama.

families.title: Bold or shameless
families.scene: নির্লজ্জ ছাত্র শূন্য পেয়েও বলল, স্যার, অটোগ্রাফটা বড় করে দিন!
families.distinctions: Audacious can be admirable; temerity and presumptuous imply overstepping; bravado can be a show of courage.

families.title: Brave or courageous
families.scene: সাহসী পিঁপড়ে হাতিকে বলল, রাস্তা ছাড়ো, আমার অফিসে দেরি হচ্ছে!
families.distinctions: Fortitude especially means endurance through adversity.

families.title: Reckless or hasty
families.scene: না ভেবেই লাফ দিল; পরে মনে পড়ল, পুলে জল দেওয়ার কাজটা বাকি!
families.distinctions: Precipitate also means cause an event; precipitous can mean steep.

families.title: Fearful or timid
families.scene: ভীতু ভূত নিজের ছায়া দেখে ওঝাকে ফোন করল!
families.distinctions: Craven strongly condemns cowardice; coy means bashful or deliberately reserved.

families.title: Cautious or watchful
families.scene: সতর্ক কাকু কলার খোসার পাশেও হেলমেট পরে হাঁটেন!
families.distinctions: Canny can also mean shrewd; discreet concerns avoiding unwanted attention.

families.title: Shrewd or perceptive
families.scene: চালাক বিড়াল মাছ চুরির আগেই বুঝল, কাকিমা আজ গোপন ক্যামেরা বসিয়েছেন!
families.distinctions: Cunning and wily suggest craftiness; acumen is keenness of judgment.

families.title: Skilled or capable
families.scene: দক্ষ রাঁধুনি চোখ বুজে লুচি বানান; লুচিরাও নিখুঁত গোল হয়ে সম্মান দেখায়!
families.distinctions: Prowess is skill or ability; nimble can describe mental or physical agility.

families.title: Flexible or adaptable
families.scene: নমনীয় রবার এমন মানিয়ে নিল যে যোগগুরু তাকেই শিক্ষক মানলেন!
families.distinctions: Versatile means having many abilities or uses; plastic also has an artificiality sense.

families.title: Stubborn or determined
families.scene: জেদি ছাগল গেটের সামনে বসে আছে—গেট খুললেও জেতার জন্য উঠবে না!
families.distinctions: Dogged and resolute are often positive; obdurate and obstinate often negative; indefatigable stresses not tiring.

families.title: Uncompromising or rigid
families.scene: একগুঁয়ে কাকু বললেন, পৃথিবী গোল মানি না; আমার মানচিত্রটা চৌকো!
families.distinctions: Implacable means unable to be appeased; dogmatic and doctrinaire concern rigid beliefs.

families.title: Changeable or erratic
families.scene: মেজাজ এমন বদলায় যে আবহাওয়া দপ্তর তার কাছেই আপডেট চায়!
families.distinctions: Whimsical can also mean playfully fanciful; volatile may suggest explosiveness.

families.title: Uncertain or hesitant
families.scene: চা নাকি কফি ভাবতে ভাবতে সন্ধ্যা হলো; শেষে দোকানটাই বন্ধ!
families.distinctions: Ambivalent means mixed feelings; incredulous means disbelieving; demur raises an objection.

families.title: Willingness or inclination
families.scene: মিষ্টির প্রতি এমন ঝোঁক যে কম্পাসের কাঁটাও রসগোল্লার দোকানে ঘোরে!
families.distinctions: Affinity can also mean a similarity or natural connection.

families.title: Strong belief or confidence
families.scene: সে এত নিশ্চিত গলায় বলল যে ভুল উত্তরটাও একটু বিশ্বাস করতে শুরু করল!
families.distinctions: Aver is to state confidently; assertive describes confident expression.

families.title: Talkative or wordy
families.scene: এত কথা বলে যে মাইক্রোফোনই বলল, দাদা এবার আমাকে বাড়ি যেতে দিন!
families.distinctions: Expatiate means discuss at length; voluble stresses fluent readiness to speak.

families.title: Quiet or reserved
families.scene: এত কম কথা বলে যে তার টিয়া পাখি নিজেই নিজের সঙ্গে আড্ডা দেয়!
families.distinctions: Recluse names a person living in isolation; aloof suggests emotional distance.

families.title: Brief or concise
families.scene: পুরো প্রেমপত্র লিখল দুই শব্দে—বিয়ে করবি? ডাকটিকিটও সাশ্রয় হলো!
families.distinctions: Pithy adds substance or force; synoptic means providing a broad summary.

families.title: Eloquent or articulate
families.scene: বক্তা এমন সুন্দর কথা বলেন যে মাইকও নোট নিতে বসে যায়!
families.distinctions: Glib is fluent but shallow or insincere; rhetoric concerns persuasive language.

families.title: Thoughtful or reflective
families.scene: শেষ সমুচাটা খাব কি না, এমন গভীর চিন্তা—সমুচারই দাড়ি গজাল!
families.distinctions: Premeditate is to plan beforehand; deliberate also means intentional.

families.title: Learned or intellectual
families.scene: এত পণ্ডিত যে বিশ্বকোষ আটকে গেলে ওঁকেই ফোন করে!
families.distinctions: Polymath and connoisseur name knowledgeable people; connoisseur concerns discerning expertise.

families.title: Naive or inexperienced
families.scene: সরল ছাগল অনলাইনে নকল ঘাস কিনে বলল, ছবিতে তো সবুজই ছিল!
families.distinctions: Gullible stresses susceptibility to deception; dilettante is an amateur with limited commitment.

families.title: Knowledge or understanding
families.scene: কৌতূহলী কাকু খবর জানতে চায়ের কাপে মাইক্রোফোন বসালেন!
families.distinctions: Ascertain means establish a fact; abreast means informed; inquisitive means eager to learn.

families.title: Teach or enlighten
families.scene: শিক্ষক বিড়ালকে পড়াতে পড়াতে এমন জ্ঞান দিলেন যে বিড়ালও হোমওয়ার্ক দিল!
families.distinctions: Didactic can suggest an overly instructive tone.

families.title: Support or reinforce
families.scene: বন্ধুর যুক্তির পক্ষে এমন প্রমাণ আনল যে টেবিলটাও সমর্থনে পা বাড়াল!
families.distinctions: Corroborate and substantiate add evidence; abet often supports wrongdoing; apologist names a defender.

families.title: Praise or admire
families.scene: লুচি গোল হয়েছে দেখে এমন প্রশংসা—রাঁধুনি নিজেই পুরস্কার বিতরণী খুললেন!
families.distinctions: Laudable, meritorious, and estimable describe what deserves praise.

families.title: Deep respect or reverence
families.scene: এমন ভক্তি যে দাদুর পুরোনো চপ্পলকেও পাড়ায় লাল কার্পেট দেওয়া হলো!
families.distinctions: Deify and canonize suggest extreme or sacred admiration; august means respected or majestic.

families.title: Improve or refine
families.scene: পুরোনো হাঁড়ি ঘষে এমন উন্নতি হলো যে সে নিজেকে পাঁচতারা হোটেল ভাবে!
families.distinctions: Remedial means corrective; convalescent describes recovering health.

families.title: Damage or undermine
families.scene: বাড়ির ভিত থেকে ইঁট চুরি করছে ইঁদুর—আড়ালে আড়ালে গোটা বাড়ি দুর্বল!
families.distinctions: Tarnish often affects reputation; adulterate reduces purity; compromise also has unrelated senses.

families.title: Worsen or aggravate
families.scene: রাগী বন্ধুকে বললাম শান্ত হও, তারপর তার লাড্ডু খেলাম—অবস্থা আরও খারাপ!
families.distinctions: Fester suggests worsening over time.

families.title: Obstruct or restrict
families.scene: পড়ার টেবিলে বিড়াল বসে এমন বাধা দিল যে কলমকেও অনুমতিপত্র লাগল!
families.distinctions: Occlude means block an opening; manacle restrains physically; circumscribe sets limits.

families.title: Prevent or avoid
families.scene: মিষ্টির দোকানে যাওয়ার আগেই মানিব্যাগ মা লুকোলেন—বিপদ আগে থেকেই ঠেকানো!
families.distinctions: Eschew, abstain, and forbear concern voluntary avoidance; forestall and foil prevent an outcome.

families.title: Destroy or remove
families.scene: ভাইরাস মুছতে গিয়ে সব গেমও উধাও—কম্পিউটার এখন একেবারে তপস্বী!
families.distinctions: Quash suppresses or voids; abrogate formally abolishes; exorcize drives something out.

families.title: Cancel or counteract
families.scene: লঙ্কার ঝাল কাটাতে দই এল; জিভে দুই দলের প্রভাব কেটে শান্তি ফিরল!
families.distinctions: Both can mean make ineffective; neutralize can mean offset an effect.

families.title: Stop or interrupt
families.scene: নল বন্ধ, জল বন্ধ; ভাইয়ের গান বন্ধ করতেও যদি এমন কল থাকত!
families.distinctions: Sever cuts a connection; stanch stops a flow.

families.title: Reject or abandon
families.scene: ভুয়া পুরস্কার ফেরত দিয়ে বলল, এর বদলে আসল রসগোল্লা দিন!
families.distinctions: Recant withdraws an earlier statement; spurn rejects contemptuously.

families.title: Dismiss or marginalize
families.scene: সভার বক্তাকে সরিয়ে শেষ বেঞ্চে বসাল—এখন মশাই তাঁর একমাত্র শ্রোতা!
families.distinctions: Relegate lowers rank; subordinate has noun, adjective, and verb senses.

families.title: Expel or remove from power
families.scene: দুষ্ট মোরগকে উঠোন থেকে তাড়িয়ে দিল; এখন প্রতিবেশীর ভোর নষ্ট হচ্ছে!
families.distinctions: Depose specifically removes someone from office or power.

families.title: Isolate or confine
families.scene: হাঁচিওয়ালা খেলনা ডাইনোসরকে আলাদা ঘরে রাখা হলো—টেডিও দূর থেকে প্রণাম করে!
families.distinctions: Quarantine isolates for disease control; immure confines or walls in.

families.title: Separate or estrange
families.scene: রসগোল্লা নিয়ে ঝগড়ার পর দুই বন্ধু এমন দূরে, মাঝে মিষ্টির দোকানও হার মানে!
families.distinctions: Alienate causes emotional separation; divorced can simply mean disconnected.

families.title: Unite or combine
families.scene: চা, দুধ আর চিনি মিলল; সবাই বলল, এবার দল বেঁধে আড্ডা চালাও!
families.distinctions: Collaborate means work jointly; collude and conspire suggest secrecy or wrongdoing; intertwined means closely linked.

families.title: Division or difference
families.scene: পাড়ায় মোহনবাগান-ইস্টবেঙ্গল তর্কে চায়ের দোকানের বেঞ্চও দুই দলে ভাগ!
families.distinctions: Antithesis is direct opposition; discrepancy is a mismatch; factious causes division.

families.title: Similarity or equivalence
families.scene: একই সাইজের দুই লুচি—একটাকে অন্যটা ভেবে নিজের ভাগটাই দুবার খেলাম!
families.distinctions: Homogeneous means made of similar parts; correlate means vary together, not necessarily be equivalent.

families.title: Mixed or diverse
families.scene: ফ্রিজের সব বাটি মিশিয়ে এমন খিচুড়ি হলো যে ভূগোল বইও ঈর্ষা করল!
families.distinctions: Cosmopolitan can also describe a sophisticated person.

families.title: Replace or substitute
families.scene: বসের বদলে টেডি বসল; কাজ একই, শুধু বিস্কুটের খরচ কম!
families.distinctions: Proxy names a substitute; fungible concerns interchangeable units of the same type.

families.title: Imitate or reproduce
families.scene: ছোট ভাই দাদার গলা নকল করতে গিয়ে পরিবারের দ্বিতীয় রেডিও হয়ে গেল!
families.distinctions: Emulate may aim to match or surpass; derivative often implies unoriginality.

families.title: Commonplace or dull
families.scene: এত একঘেয়ে গল্প যে ঘুমের ওষুধ এসে বলল, আমার চাকরি খাবেন নাকি?
families.distinctions: Platitude is a trite remark; ennui is the feeling of boredom.

families.title: Unusual or unconventional
families.scene: লোকটা ছাতা পায়ে পরে বেরোল—আজব স্টাইল দেখে বৃষ্টিও থমকে গেল!
families.distinctions: Unprecedented means never previously seen; exotic suggests foreignness; fringe suggests being outside the mainstream.

families.title: Unorthodox or rebellious
families.scene: পুরোনো নিয়ম ভেঙে ছাত্র বলল, এবার শিক্ষক হোমওয়ার্ক করবেন—ক্লাসে বিদ্রোহ!
families.distinctions: Heterodox concerns beliefs; mutiny is rebellion against authority; dissent is disagreement.

families.title: Limited outlook
families.scene: পাড়ার বাইরেও পৃথিবী আছে শুনে কাকু বললেন, ওখানে কি আমাদের চায়ের দোকান আছে?
families.distinctions: Myopic stresses short-sightedness; insular and parochial stress restricted perspective.

families.title: Trivial or unimportant
families.scene: জামার একটি সুতো নিয়ে এমন আলোচনা—আসল জামাটাই বিরক্ত হয়ে চলে গেল!
families.distinctions: Frivolous may describe an unserious person; nominal can mean in name only.

families.title: Irrelevant or unnecessary
families.scene: অঙ্কের উত্তরে মশার জীবনী লিখেছি—বাড়তি তো বটেই, পুরো অপ্রাসঙ্গিক!
families.distinctions: Gratuitous means unwarranted; tangential is only indirectly relevant.

families.title: Relevant or suitable
families.scene: চপের সঙ্গে মুড়ি এত মানানসই যে প্লেট নিজেই বিয়ের তারিখ ঠিক করল!
families.distinctions: Appropriate also means take for oneself; felicitous can mean pleasing.

families.title: Necessary or central
families.scene: মোবাইলের চার্জার ছাড়া সব আছে; মোবাইল বলল, আসল লোকটাই অনুপস্থিত!
families.distinctions: Intrinsic and inborn mean inherent; prime means primary or prepare; fulcrum is a pivotal element.

families.title: Basic or elementary
families.scene: এমন প্রাথমিক অঙ্ক যে ক্যালকুলেটর বলল, আঙুলগুলোকে একটু কাজ করতে দিন!
families.distinctions: Both concern fundamentals or early development.

families.title: Model or ideal example
families.scene: স্যারের আদর্শ ছাত্র রোবট; ঘণ্টা বাজার আগেই নিজেকে হোমওয়ার্ক জমা দেয়!
families.distinctions: Paragon suggests excellence; archetype is a typical original model.

families.title: Deep insight or wisdom
families.scene: দাদুর জ্ঞান এত গভীর যে কুয়োও তাঁকে গভীরতার পরামর্শ চায়!
families.distinctions: Both concern depth of understanding.

families.title: Practical or workable
families.scene: কাগজের নৌকা পুকুরে চলে; চাঁদে পাঠালে নয়—কাজটা বাস্তবে সম্ভব হতে হবে!
families.distinctions: Expedient can sacrifice long-term interests; conducive helps an outcome; efficacious means effective.

families.title: Unrealistic or ineffective
families.scene: মশা তাড়াতে চাঁদে বাড়ি বানাব—কল্পনা বড়, কিন্তু পকেটে দশ টাকা!
families.distinctions: Remote here means unlikely; futile means unable to achieve a worthwhile result.

families.title: Dangerous or risky
families.scene: ভাঙা টুলে উঠে সিলিং ফ্যান মোছা—টুল বলছে, বিমাটা করিয়ে এসেছেন তো?
families.distinctions: Jeopardize puts at risk; ominous suggests coming trouble; liability creates a disadvantage.

families.title: Difficult or burdensome
families.scene: এমন কঠিন কাজ যে পাহাড়ও দেখে বলল, আমাকে উঠতেই বরং সহজ!
families.distinctions: Predicament is a difficult situation; quandary stresses uncertainty about a decision.

families.title: Fragile or weak
families.scene: বিস্কুটটা এত দুর্বল যে চায়ে নামার আগেই উইল লিখে গেল!
families.distinctions: Tenuous means thin or weak, often of a connection or claim.

families.title: Strong or resilient
families.scene: হাজারবার পড়েও খেলনা হাঁস হাসছে—এমন শক্ত মন দেখে জিমে ডাক পড়ল!
families.distinctions: Resilient recovers after difficulty; redoubtable inspires respect or fear.

families.title: Defeat or overcome
families.scene: বাধা পেরিয়ে ছাগল পাহাড়ে উঠল; পাহাড়ই শেষে বলল, তুই জিতেছিস!
families.distinctions: Vanquish defeats; surmount overcomes; outstrip and eclipse surpass; transcend goes beyond limits.

families.title: Yield or give in
families.scene: ডায়েটের সঙ্গে যুদ্ধ শেষে জিলিপির কাছে আত্মসমর্পণ করলাম—সাদা পতাকাও মিষ্টি!
families.distinctions: Yield also means produce; relent can mean become less severe.

families.title: Forgive or clear of blame
families.scene: কেক চুরির দোষ কাটল; ভিডিওতে দেখা গেল টেডি নয়, রোবট খেয়েছে!
families.distinctions: Condone overlooks an act; exculpate and exonerate remove blame.

families.title: Disprove or challenge
families.scene: প্রমাণ দিলাম ভূত নয়, জানালার পর্দা—ভূতের চাকরিটাই ভুয়া প্রমাণিত!
families.distinctions: Impugn questions validity or character; gainsay contradicts; refute and debunk disprove.

families.title: Wrongdoing or violation
families.scene: নিয়ম ভেঙে মোরগ লাইনে আগে ঢুকল; ডিমের দোকানেই তার বিচার বসল!
families.distinctions: Peccadillo is minor; malfeasance often involves officials; perpetrate means commit an act.

families.title: Betrayal or broken promise
families.scene: একটি লাড্ডুও খাব না বলে পুরো হাঁড়ি খালি—প্রতিশ্রুতি গেল পেটের ভেতর!
families.distinctions: Perfidy is treachery; renege means fail to honor a commitment.

families.title: Force or compel
families.scene: চকলেট আটকে মা বললেন পড়তে বসো—ভাই বলল, এ তো মিষ্টি জোরজবরদস্তি!
families.distinctions: Dictate can mean command; duress is pressure by threat or force.

families.title: Mock virtue or devotion
families.scene: নিজেকে সাধু বলে বক্তৃতা দিচ্ছেন, আর আড়ালে আমার শেষ সন্দেশটা খাচ্ছেন!
families.distinctions: Pious can mean sincerely devout; sanctimonious is negatively self-righteous.

families.title: Physical or worldly
families.scene: ধ্যানে আত্মা ভাবছে মহাবিশ্ব; শরীর ভাবছে আলুর দম—পার্থিব ব্যাপার আলাদা!
families.distinctions: Corporeal concerns the body; temporal can also concern time.

families.title: Evidence or observation
families.scene: বিড়াল দুধ খেয়েছে কি না আন্দাজ নয়—ক্যামেরা আর গোঁফের দুধই প্রমাণ!
families.distinctions: Empirical is based on observation; documentary concerns records or factual events.

families.title: Personal or biased judgment
families.scene: নিজের মায়ের রান্নাই সেরা বলে বিচারক সব ট্রফি নিজের বাড়ি পাঠালেন!
families.distinctions: Invidious can also mean causing resentment or envy.

families.title: Fair or impartial
families.scene: নিরপেক্ষ বিড়াল দুই দলের মাছ সমান ভাগ করল—নিজের জন্য একটাও রাখল না!
families.distinctions: Disinterested means unbiased, not uninterested.

families.title: Predict or foreshadow
families.scene: হাঁড়ি দেখেই বুঝলেন আজ বিরিয়ানি—ভবিষ্যৎবক্তা নাকের চাকরি জমজমাট!
families.distinctions: Extrapolate projects from existing data; harbinger is a sign of what is coming.

families.title: Good fortune or favorable conditions
families.scene: ভুল বাসে উঠে বিনামূল্যের মিষ্টির মেলায় নামলাম—এমন ভুল রোজ হোক!
families.distinctions: Fortuitous stresses chance; serendipitous adds fortunate discovery; boon is a benefit.

families.title: Highest point
families.scene: সাফল্যের চূড়ায় উঠে কাকু দেখলেন, সেখানেও চায়ের দোকানে লাইন!
families.distinctions: Crescendo is associated with rising loudness and, in the PDF, the highest point.

families.title: Small or scarce
families.scene: প্লেটে এত কম ভাত যে পিঁপড়ে বলল, এটা আমারও ডায়েটের খাবার!
families.distinctions: Diminutive and minute concern size; scant, sparse, and dearth concern insufficient quantity or density.

families.title: Large or excessive
families.scene: এত প্রশ্নের ঢল নামল যে শিক্ষক ছাতার বদলে অভিধান মাথায় ধরলেন!
families.distinctions: Surfeit is excess; inundate overwhelms; barrage is a concentrated onslaught.

families.title: Draw out or evoke
families.scene: স্কুলের ঘণ্টা বাজতেই টিফিনের স্মৃতি জাগল—পেটই প্রথম উত্তর দিল!
families.distinctions: Elicit draws a response out; evoke brings a feeling or memory to mind.

families.title: Create or prepare
families.scene: বক্তৃতা তৈরি নেই; কাকু তখনই নতুন শব্দ বানিয়ে মাইককেই মুগ্ধ করলেন!
families.distinctions: Coin invents a term; improvise and extemporize act without preparation; prime prepares for action.

families.title: Consequence or result
families.scene: মিথ্যা অসুখ বলে ছুটি নিলাম; ফল হলো মা আসলেই তেতো ওষুধ খাওয়ালেন!
families.distinctions: Repercussion commonly suggests an unintended, negative consequence.

families.title: Emphasize
families.scene: গুরুত্ব বোঝাতে স্যার এত দাগ দিলেন যে খাতাই বলল, এবার বুঝেছি!
families.distinctions: Both draw attention to importance.

families.title: Imply without stating
families.scene: বস শুধু খালি কাপ দেখালেন; সবাই বুঝল চা চাই—মুখে কিছু বলতেই হলো না!
families.distinctions: Allusive makes indirect references; intimate is a verb in this sense.

families.title: Exaggerate or embellish
families.scene: মাছটা এত বড় ছিল বলে গল্প করল যে অ্যাকুয়ারিয়াম বর্ধিত বাজেট চাইল!
families.distinctions: Embellish may literally decorate or figuratively add invented detail.

families.title: Figurative expression
families.scene: স্যারকে বাঘ বললাম; তিনি মাংস নয়, হোমওয়ার্ক চাইলেন—এটা রূপক ছিল!
families.distinctions: Euphemism substitutes a milder expression; it need not be metaphorical.

families.title: Understated or delicate
families.scene: নিজের জয় ঘোষণা করল শুধু ছোট্ট হাসিতে—ঢাকও কাজ না পেয়ে মনখারাপ করল!
families.distinctions: Modest can describe humility or limited scale.

families.title: Attractive style or taste
families.scene: এমন রুচিশীল সাজ যে চায়ের কাপও নিজের জন্য সানগ্লাস কিনল!
families.distinctions: Panache is stylish confidence; poise is composure or balance; modish is fashionable; piquant is stimulating.

families.title: Humor or lightness
families.scene: গম্ভীর সভায় টিয়াটা কৌতুক বলল—সভাপতির গোঁফও হাসি চাপতে পারল না!
families.distinctions: Facetious and levity can suggest inappropriate joking.

families.title: Sentimental expression
families.scene: পুরোনো বাসের টিকিট দেখে এমন আবেগ—টিকিট চেকারও প্রেমের গান ধরলেন!
families.distinctions: Mawkish is excessively sentimental; croon means sing softly; rhapsody is an ecstatic expression.

families.title: Sexual or indulgent interests
families.scene: আড্ডার কাকু সব গল্পেই এমন দুষ্টু ইঙ্গিত খোঁজেন যে ফুলও লজ্জায় পাতা ঢাকে!
families.distinctions: Bawdy concerns sexual humor; prurient concerns excessive sexual interest; libertine names a pleasure-seeker.

families.title: Cruel or emotionally insensitive
families.scene: ভিলেন অন্যের কান্নায় হাসে; নায়ক বলল, হাসির সাবস্ক্রিপশনটা বড় নিষ্ঠুর!
families.distinctions: Sadistic enjoys suffering; callous lacks sensitivity; malevolent wishes harm.

families.title: Loud or harsh sound
families.scene: এমন কর্কশ কোলাহল যে মাইক্রোফোন নিজেই কানের তুলো কিনল!
families.distinctions: Vociferous concerns forceful expression; obstreperous also means unruly.

families.title: Awkward or unskilled socially
families.scene: আনমনা অতিথি করমর্দনের বদলে দরজার হাতল নাড়লেন—সবার সামনে অপ্রস্তুত!
families.distinctions: Gawky commonly includes physical awkwardness.

families.title: Pure or unspoiled
families.scene: শার্ট এত নির্মল যে ধুলোকণা ঢোকার আগে জুতো খুলে অনুমতি চাইল!
families.distinctions: Inviolate means not violated; immaculate also means without errors.

families.title: Separation from reality or logic
families.scene: বরফ বিক্রেতা বলল, আমার গরম বরফ খুব ঠান্ডা—বেমানান কথায় মাথায় ধোঁয়া!
families.distinctions: Incongruous means out of place; paradoxical seems contradictory but may be true.

families.title: Occasional or irregular
families.scene: পাড়ার কলের জল মাঝে মাঝে আসে—কলটা বুঝি অতিথি শিল্পী!
families.distinctions: Both contrast with continuous occurrence.

families.title: Random or unplanned
families.scene: পরিকল্পনা ছাড়া সব রান্না এক হাঁড়িতে—লুচি এখন ডালের সঙ্গে ভবিষ্যৎ খুঁজছে!
families.distinctions: Arbitrary is not based on reason; indiscriminate lacks selectivity; desultory lacks sustained direction.

families.title: Order or rank
families.scene: অফিসে পদমর্যাদার ধাপ এত যে শেষ কর্মী বসকে দেখতে দূরবিন আনল!
families.distinctions: Echelon is a level in a hierarchy; subordinate is lower in rank.

families.title: Tolerate or permit
families.scene: দারোয়ান ঢুকতে অনুমতি দিলেন, কিন্তু নিয়ম ভাঙতেই জরিমানা—এক শব্দে দুটো উল্টো কাজ!
families.distinctions: Sanction has opposite senses: authorize and penalize; countenance also means facial expression.

families.title: Repulsive or offensive
families.scene: এমন দুর্গন্ধ যে নিজের মোজাও নাক চেপে অন্য ঘরে পালাল!
families.distinctions: Both imply strong dislike or disgust.

families.title: Disturb or embarrass
families.scene: মাইকে নাম ভুল বলতেই বক্তা এমন বিব্রত—মাইককেও আত্মপরিচয় দিতে হলো!
families.distinctions: Agitate excites or disturbs; discomfit makes uneasy or embarrassed.

families.title: Foresight or imagination
families.scene: দূরদর্শী কাকু বৃষ্টি আসার আগেই নৌকায় চায়ের দোকান খুললেন!
families.distinctions: Visionary can also mean imaginative; prophetic and prescient emphasize foresight.

families.title: Working hard
families.scene: পরিশ্রমী পিঁপড়ে ছুটির দিনেও বাদামের হিসাব করে—অ্যালার্ম তার কাছেই শেখে!
families.distinctions: Industrious stresses effort; sedulous diligence; indefatigable tirelessness.

families.title: Supplement or support
families.scene: এক পাটি চপ্পল একা কাঁদছিল; অন্য পাটি এসে বলল, এবার জুটি সম্পূর্ণ!
families.distinctions: Auxiliary is additional support; complementary completes something else.

families.title: Inflated or convoluted expression
families.scene: সহজ কথাকে এত ফুলিয়ে বলল যে বক্তৃতার জন্য আলাদা বেলুন লাগল!
families.distinctions: Turgid also means swollen; its prose sense suggests overblown complexity.

families.title: Childish or immature
families.scene: বড় ভাই খেলনা গাড়ি না পেয়ে কাঁদছে; ছোট ভাই তার অভিভাবক হয়ে গেল!
families.distinctions: Puerile criticizes childish behavior; callow stresses inexperience.

families.title: Urgent or essential
families.scene: জরুরি চার্জার আনো—মোবাইল এক শতাংশ ব্যাটারিতে শেষ চিঠি লিখছে!
families.distinctions: Exigent requires immediate action; indispensable means essential.

families.title: Unproductive
families.scene: জমি ফাঁকা পড়ে আছে; বীজ বলল, আমাকে না ফেললে ফসলের চাকরি হবে কী করে?
families.distinctions: Fallow describes uncultivated land or inactivity, not necessarily an inability to produce.

families.title: Hypothetical or uncertain
families.scene: প্রমাণ নেই, তবু আন্দাজ করছে—ছাগল নাকি গোপনে পাইলটের প্রশিক্ষণ নেয়!
families.distinctions: Conjectural is based on limited evidence; suspect is viewed with suspicion.

families.title: Disorderly emotional display
families.scene: ওয়াই-ফাই গেলেই এমন নাটকীয় কান্না—রাউটার নিজের জন্য অস্কার দাবি করল!
families.distinctions: Hysterical is wildly emotional; histrionic is excessively theatrical.

families.title: Unconventional or deviating
families.scene: সবাই সোজা লাইনে, সে উল্টো হাঁটছে—নিজের নিয়মে আলাদা অভিযান!
families.distinctions: Deviate is the verb; aberrant departs from a norm; heterodox concerns accepted beliefs.

families.title: abscond
families.scene: রসগোল্লা চুরি করে এমন চুপিচুপি পালাল যে নিজের ছায়াকেও লোকেশন দিল না!
families.distinctions: leave hurriedly and secretly, typically to avoid capture

families.title: abstract
families.scene: মাথার আইডিয়াটা হাতে ধরতে গিয়ে মুঠোয় শুধু বাতাস—ভাবনা তো বিমূর্ত!
families.distinctions: Conceptual rather than physical; also to remove or isolate something.

families.title: acolyte
families.scene: গুরুর সহকারী তোতা সারাদিন গুরুর কথাই বলে—এমন অনুগামী চাই কার না!
families.distinctions: a person who assists or follows another person or cause

families.title: anoint
families.scene: বিড়ালকে পাহারাদার পদে বসালাম; মনোনয়ন পেয়ে সে প্রথমেই দুধ দপ্তর নিল!
families.distinctions: appoint or designate for a particular role or purpose

families.title: antedate
families.scene: দাদুর ডায়েরি আমার জন্মের আগের—ডায়েরিই বলে, বয়সে আমি সিনিয়র!
families.distinctions: occur before (something) in time

families.title: apprise
families.scene: আপুকে খবর জানাও, কেক এসেছে—খবর দেওয়ার আগেই আপু প্লেট নিয়ে হাজির!
families.distinctions: inform, notify, or advise

families.title: ascribe
families.scene: হাঁচির কৃতিত্ব মরিচকে দিলাম; মরিচ বলল, অবশেষে আমার কাজের স্বীকৃতি!
families.distinctions: attribute or credit something to a particular cause or source

families.title: belie
families.scene: হাসিমুখ দেখে সুখী ভাবলাম; ভেতরে শেষ চপ হারানোর শোক—মুখ আসলটা ঢাকল!
families.distinctions: give a false impression of; mask

families.title: bucolic
families.scene: শান্ত গ্রামের গরু বাঁশি শুনছে; শহরের হর্ন এসে বলল, আমিও কি ছুটি পাই?
families.distinctions: associated with tranquil rural life

families.title: cataclysmic
families.scene: চা উল্টে ল্যাপটপ গেল—ডেস্কে এমন বিপর্যয় যে পিঁপড়েও উদ্ধারদল ডাকল!
families.distinctions: causing great disruption or upheaval

families.title: cathartic
families.scene: সিরিয়াল দেখে কেঁদে মন হালকা; টিস্যুর বাক্স বলল, কাউন্সেলিংয়ের বিল আমি দেব?
families.distinctions: that which releases emotional tension

families.title: chauvinistic
families.scene: নিজের ক্লাবই মহাবিশ্বের সেরা বলে কাকু মঙ্গলগ্রহের দলকেও পাত্তা দেন না!
families.distinctions: excessively patriotic or biased in favor of a group or cause

families.title: coddle
families.scene: বাচ্চা বিড়ালকে এত আদর যে নিজে হাঁটতে ভুলে ব্যক্তিগত গাড়ি চাইল!
families.distinctions: pamper or treat with excessive care

families.title: commence
families.scene: পড়াশোনা শুরু করতেই এমন উদ্বোধন—খাতার সামনে ফিতে কাটা হলো!
families.distinctions: begin or start

families.title: commiserate
families.scene: বন্ধুর চপ পড়ে গেছে; পাশে বসে দুজনেই চপের আত্মার জন্য দীর্ঘশ্বাস ফেলি!
families.distinctions: express sympathy or sorrow with someone who has experienced misfortune

families.title: conflagration
families.scene: রান্নার আগুন এমন ছড়াল যে ফায়ার অ্যালার্মও ছুটির আবেদন করল!
families.distinctions: a large, destructive fire

families.title: consensus
families.scene: চার বন্ধু একমত হলো বিরিয়ানি খাবে—এই ঐকমত্যই দলের একমাত্র সংবিধান!
families.distinctions: general agreement among the members of a group

families.title: construe
families.scene: স্যার বললেন বসো; আমি অর্থ করলাম বিশ্রাম নাও—ব্যাখ্যার স্বাধীনতায় ঘুমিয়ে পড়লাম!
families.distinctions: understand something subjectively

families.title: contend
families.scene: ছাগল দাবি করছে সে গায়ক; মঞ্চ পেতে লড়ছে, আর মোরগের সঙ্গে প্রতিযোগিতাও করছে!
families.distinctions: Argue or assert; also compete or struggle.

families.title: contrite
families.scene: শেষ মিষ্টি খেয়ে এত অনুতপ্ত যে খালি প্লেটের কাছেই ক্ষমা চাইল!
families.distinctions: feeling regretful or guilty

families.title: conventional
families.scene: সবাই যেমন করে তেমনই বিয়ে—মেনু বদলাতেই কাকুর প্রচলিত নিয়মে ভূমিকম্প!
families.distinctions: adhering to established practices or accepted standards

families.title: curmudgeon
families.scene: খিটখিটে কাকু মেঘকেও বকেন—বৃষ্টি দিলে ভেজায়, না দিলে গরম করে!
families.distinctions: An ill-tempered person.

families.title: desiccate
families.scene: দেশি ক্যাট রোদে এত শুকোল যে তার গোঁফও শুকনো নুডলস হয়ে গেল!
families.distinctions: dry out; remove all moisture

families.title: digression
families.scene: স্যার অঙ্ক শুরু করে নিজের বিয়ের গল্পে গেলেন—সমীকরণও মূল প্রসঙ্গ খুঁজছে!
families.distinctions: an aside that strays from the main subject

families.title: dispense
families.scene: মেশিন লাড্ডু বিলি করে; ডায়েটে বললাম লাড্ডু বাদ দাও—বিলি আর বাদ, দুটো মনে রাখো!
families.distinctions: 1. issue, distribute, or give out 2. do without or get rid of

families.title: distill
families.scene: দশ পাতার বক্তৃতা ছেঁকে পাওয়া গেল আসল কথা: টাকা ধার দাও!
families.distinctions: extract the most important information from something

families.title: distort
families.scene: সেলফির ফিল্টার নাক এত বদলে দিল যে পাসপোর্ট নিজেকেই সন্দেহ করল!
families.distinctions: give a false or misleading account of

families.title: egregious
families.scene: লবণের বদলে পুরো সাবান দিয়ে রান্না—এমন ভয়ানক ভুলে তরকারিও ফেনায় প্রতিবাদ করে!
families.distinctions: Exceptionally bad or shocking.

families.title: elitist
families.scene: নিজেকে এত অভিজাত ভাবে যে লিফটেও শুধু উপরের তলার বোতাম টেপে!
families.distinctions: 1. a person who believes in the rule of an elite or privileged group 2. believing oneself or a group to be superior to others

families.title: encroach
families.scene: পাশের লাউগাছ ধীরে আমার বারান্দা দখল করছে—পরের মাসে বুঝি ভাড়া চাইবে!
families.distinctions: intrude or trespass, especially on another's territory or rights

families.title: endemic
families.scene: এই পাড়াতেই ওই বিশেষ মশা থাকে—বাইরে গেলে নাকি স্থানীয় ভাতা মেলে না!
families.distinctions: regularly found and restricted to a particular area or population

families.title: endow
families.scene: পরি বিড়ালকে কথা বলার ক্ষমতা দিলেন; এখন সে দুধের বাজেট নিয়ে বক্তৃতা দেয়!
families.distinctions: enrich or furnish with some faculty or quality

families.title: expedite
families.scene: ফাইল দ্রুত করাতে এমন তাড়া দিলাম যে স্ট্যাপলারও দৌড়ের জুতো পরল!
families.distinctions: accelerate or speed up a process or action

families.title: fallible
families.scene: ক্যালকুলেটরও ভুল করল—মেশিনও বলছে, আমাকে দেবতা ভেবো না!
families.distinctions: capable of making an error

families.title: gaffe

questions.prompt:
*ETS Official Guide — Chapter 4, Set 1, original question 2*

**Choose one answer.**

Kagan maintains that an infant’s reactions to its first stressful experiences are part of a natural process of development, not harbingers of childhood unhappiness or ________ signs of adolescent anxiety.

- **A.** prophetic
- **B.** normal
- **C.** monotonous
- **D.** virtual
- **E.** typical
questions.stem:
*ETS Official Guide — Chapter 4, Set 1, original question 2*

**Choose one answer.**

Kagan maintains that an infant’s reactions to its first stressful experiences are part of a natural process of development, not harbingers of childhood unhappiness or ________ signs of adolescent anxiety.
questions.explanation:
The sentence contrasts the infant’s reactions, part of a normal developmental process, with future unhappiness and anxiety. The missing word describes signs of adolescent anxiety as they relate to the infant. Choice A is correct: “prophetic” signs, like harbingers, foretell future occurrences, and for the infant, adolescent anxiety is a future occurrence. Since an infant cannot literally display signs of adolescent anxiety, “normal,” “monotonous,” and “typical” are all incorrect. And “virtual” is incorrect, because virtual signs are not real signs, and what Kagan is denying is that the infant’s reactions are not real signs of later unhappiness.

Thus the correct answer is prophetic (Choice A).

*Explanation: [ETS Official Guide](gre_data/sources/ets.pdf), PDF p. 115.*

| Blank (i) | Blank (ii) | Blank (iii) |
| --- | --- | --- |

questions.stem:
*ETS Official Guide — Chapter 4, Set 3, original question 5*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

Statements presented as fact in a patent application are (i) ________ unless a good reason for doubt is found. The invention has only to be deemed “more likely than not” to work in order to receive initial approval. And, although thousands of patents are challenged in court for other reasons, no incentive exists for anyone to expend effort (ii) ________ the science of an erroneous patent. For this reason the endless stream of (iii) ________ devices will continue to yield occasional patents.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): A. presumed verifiable**
- **Blank (ii): F. debunking**
- **Blank (iii): H. bogus**
questions.explanation:
The paragraph appears to be explaining some odd or unexpected aspect of the patent process. The third sentence helps to clarify what this aspect is; it discusses challenges to patents. The only choice for Blank (ii) that is concerned with challenging a patent is “debunking,” since “corroborating” and “advancing” suggest support instead. This in turn provides the answer for the third blank, since the preceding sentence does explain how “bogus” devices may nonetheless get a patent. And we can also now better understand the first sentence — it too must help explain how bogus devices get patents, which it can do only if the blank is filled with “presumed verifiable,” suggesting that patent applications are taken at face value and not dismissed out of hand nor subjected to careful scrutiny.

Thus the correct answer is presumed verifiable (Choice A), debunking (Choice F), and bogus (Choice H).

*Explanation: [ETS Official Guide](gre_data/sources/ets.pdf), PDF p. 131.*

questions.stem:
*ETS Official Guide — Chapter 4, Set 5, original question 2*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

Human nature and long distances have made exceeding the speed limit a (i) ________ in the state, so the legislators surprised no one when, acceding to public demand, they (ii) ________ increased penalties for speeding.

Thus the correct answer is belies (Choice A) and a cautious (Choice F).

*Explanation: [ETS Official Guide](gre_data/sources/ets.pdf), PDF p. 144.*

questions.stem:
*ETS Official Guide — Chapter 4, Set 5, original question 5*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

Managers who think that strong environmental performance will (i) ________ their company’s financial performance often (ii) ________ claims that systems designed to help them manage environmental concerns are valuable tools. By contrast, managers who perceive environmental performance to be (iii) ________ to financial success may view an environmental management system as extraneous. In either situation, and whatever their perceptions, it is a manager’s commitment to achieving environmental improvement rather than the mere presence of a system that determines environmental performance.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): B. bolster**
- **Blank (ii): D. uncritically accept**
- **Blank (iii): I. peripheral**
questions.explanation:
The first two sentences introduce two contrasting sets of managers. The managers identified in the second sentence view systems designed to help manage environmental concerns as “extraneous,” suggesting that they would view environmental performance to be “peripheral” (Choice I) to financial performance. The other options for Blank (iii) — “complementary” and “intrinsic” — are not consistent with the idea that environmental management systems are extraneous. With Blank (iii) filled in, we can go back to Blanks (i) and (ii) with greater confidence: “bolster” works best in Blank (i), since the two sets of managers have contrasting views. Blank (ii) is not straightforward — clearly these managers would not “hotly dispute” this claim, but “appropriately acknowledge” is less easily ruled out. “Uncritically accept” makes sense and is confirmed when we look at the final sentence in which the author warns that, in either situation, “the mere presence of a system” is not enough to achieve environmental improvement. In fact, a system is not even necessary. Thus the author of the paragraph does not regard the systems as particularly valuable, ruling out “appropriately acknowledge.”

Thus the correct answer is bolster (Choice B), uncritically accept (Choice D), and peripheral (Choice I).

*Explanation: [ETS Official Guide](gre_data/sources/ets.pdf), PDF p. 146.*

Philosophy, unlike most other subjects, does not try to extend our knowledge by discovering new information about the world. Instead it tries to deepen our understanding through (i) ________ what is already closest to us — the experiences, thoughts, concepts, and activities that make up our lives but that ordinarily escape our notice precisely because they are so familiar. Philosophy begins by finding (ii) ________ the things that are (iii) ________.

| Blank (i) | Blank (ii) | Blank (iii) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A.** attainment of | **D.** essentially irrelevant | **G.** most prosaic |
| **B.** rumination on | **E.** utterly mysterious | **H.** somewhat hackneyed |
| **C.** detachment from | **F.** thoroughly commonplace | **I.** refreshingly novel |
questions.stem:
*ETS Official Guide — Chapter 4, Set 5, original question 6*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

Philosophy, unlike most other subjects, does not try to extend our knowledge by discovering new information about the world. Instead it tries to deepen our understanding through (i) ________ what is already closest to us — the experiences, thoughts, concepts, and activities that make up our lives but that ordinarily escape our notice precisely because they are so familiar. Philosophy begins by finding (ii) ________ the things that are (iii) ________.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): B. rumination on**
- **Blank (ii): E. utterly mysterious**
- **Blank (iii): G. most prosaic**
questions.explanation:
The first two sentences present a contrast between extending our knowledge by discovering “new information about the world” — which we are told philosophy does not do — and extending knowledge through some activity involving “things that are closest to us.” The first blank asks us to identify that activity, and although “attainment” makes little sense in context, both “rumination on” and “detachment from” have some appeal. However, the clear implication that philosophy attends to things that ordinarily escape our notice eliminates “detachment from” as a correct answer. Blank (ii) requires something that suggests the importance of familiar things as subjects of philosophical rumination, and “utterly mysterious” does just that. “Essentially irrelevant” and “thoroughly commonplace” do not fit logically since they suggest that these “familiar” things are unimportant. Similarly, Blank (iii) needs to be consistent with the description of those things as familiar and close. “Most prosaic” fits that idea while “refreshingly novel” goes in the other direction. “Somewhat hackneyed” has some plausibility but is too negative given the overall tone of the sentence; there is no indication that those things are in any way trite.

Thus the correct answer is rumination on (Choice B), utterly mysterious (Choice E), and most prosaic (Choice G).

*Explanation: [ETS Official Guide](gre_data/sources/ets.pdf), PDF pp. 147–148.*

questions.stem:
*ETS Official Guide — Practice Test 1, Section 3, original question 16*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

Belanger dances with an (i) ________ that draws one’s attention as if by seeking to (ii) ________ it; through finesse and understatement, he manages to seem at once intensely present and curiously detached.
questions.explanation:
The point of the sentence is to emphasize contradictory aspects of Belanger’s dancing: we are told, for example, that he seems “at once intensely present and curiously detached.” Looking at the second blank with this point in mind, we can see that the sentence is saying that Belanger draws attention in some way that would not normally be a means of doing so. The only choice that fits, therefore, is “deflect”; focusing or overwhelming attention would certainly be expected to draw it. And since employing “unrestrained enthusiasm” or “unattractive gawkiness” would not be ways of deflecting attention, the correct choice for the first blank is “undemonstrative panache,” another paradoxical term, since “panache” means “dash or flamboyance in style.” Thus, the correct answer is undemonstrative panache (Choice A) and deflect (Choice F).

*Explanation: [ETS Official Guide](gre_data/sources/ets.pdf), PDF p. 556.*

questions.stem:

**Choose one option for each blank.**

The discovery suggested that strong political action to halt production of CFCs might be (i) ________, and fortunately, the chemical industry no longer felt compelled to oppose such action: although companies had recently (ii) ________ their research into CFC substitutes, studies they had initiated years earlier had produced (iii) ________ results.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): A. imminent**
- **Blank (ii): F. curtailed**
- **Blank (iii): G. encouraging**
questions.explanation:
According to the first sentence, chemical companies opposed a ban on CFCs and then changed their stance in 1985 with the discovery of an ozone hole. In the first blank, only “imminent” is compatible with the discovery of an ozone hole linked to CFCs: such a discovery would suggest that “strong political action” is required, not that it is “imprudent” or “premature.” What follows the colon in the second sentence explains why the chemical industry “no longer felt compelled to oppose” a ban on CFCs. In order for the industry to drop its opposition, the outcome of the studies into CFC substitutes must have been positive. Among the choices for the third blank, only “encouraging” has a sufficiently positive connotation. Finally, the word “although” after the colon indicates that the second blank should contrast with the third blank in some way. Since the completed third blank now indicates that studies of CFC substitutes have been successful, “curtailed” makes the most sense in the second blank. “Corroborated” and “publicized” do not contrast appropriately with the success of the studies. Thus, the correct answer is imminent (Choice A); curtailed (Choice F); and encouraging (Choice G).

*Explanation: [ETS Official Guide](gre_data/sources/ets.pdf), PDF pp. 727–728.*

| Blank (i) | Blank (ii) | Blank (iii) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A.** overshadowed | **D.** enhance | **G.** plausibility of our hypotheses |

He emphasizes the enormous gaps in our knowledge, the sparseness of our observations, and the (iii) ________, calling attention to the many aspects of planetary evolution that must be better understood before we can accurately diagnose the condition of our planet.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): A. overshadowed**
- **Blank (ii): E. obscure**
- **Blank (iii): I. superficiality of our theories**
questions.explanation:
The overall tone of the passage is clearly complimentary. To understand what the author of the book is being complimented on, it is useful to focus on the second blank. Here, we must determine what word would indicate something that the author is praised for not permitting. The only answer choice that fits the case is “obscure,” since enhancing and underscoring are generally good things to do, not things one should refrain from doing. Choosing “obscure” clarifies the choice for the first blank; the only choice that fits well with “obscure” is “overshadowed.” Notice that trying to fill blank (i) without filling blank (ii) first is very hard—each choice has at least some initial plausibility. Since the third blank requires a phrase that matches “enormous gaps” and “sparseness of our observations,” the best choice is “superficiality of our theories.”

Thus the correct answer is overshadowed (Choice A), obscure (Choice E), and superficiality of our theories (Choice I).

*Explanation: [Official GRE Verbal Reasoning](gre_data/sources/verbal.pdf), PDF p. 27.*

questions.stem:
*Official GRE Verbal Reasoning — TC Practice Set 1, original question 4*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

The figure-skating pair’s convincing victory last week was particularly (i) ________ to their rivals, who were in peak form and complained privately about the judging. That the pair won when their rivals were (ii) ________ too is also impressive.
questions.explanation:
The fact that the winning pair’s rivals were “in peak physical form” suggests that these rivals had a reasonable expectation of victory; the fact that they “complained about the judging” indicates that they regarded the pair’s victory as not completely deserved. These two considerations suggest that the rivals had a negative reaction to the winning pair’s victory; the only answer choice for Blank (i) that matches this meaning is “irksome,” so it is correct. The second sentence reinforces the implication that the rivals were also strongly deserving of victory, and the word “too” suggests that the performances of the winning pair and of their rivals were comparable in quality. This points to “terrific” as the correct answer choice for Blank (ii).

Thus the correct answer is irksome (Choice B) and terrific (Choice D).

*Explanation: [Official GRE Verbal Reasoning](gre_data/sources/verbal.pdf), PDF p. 80.*

questions.explanation:

Thus the correct answer is exacted a toll (Choice A) and tepid (Choice E).

*Official GRE Verbal Reasoning — TC Practice Set 2, original question 8*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

The reason minimum temperatures are going up more rapidly than maximums may involve cloud cover and evaporative cooling. Clouds tend to keep the days cooler by reflecting sunlight, and the nights warmer by (i) ________ loss of heat from Earth’s surface. Greater amounts of moisture in the soil from additional precipitation and cloudiness (ii) ________ the daytime temperature increases because part of the solar energy is (iii) ________ the evaporation of that moisture.

| Blank (i) | Blank (ii) | Blank (iii) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A.** inhibiting | **D.** augment | **G.** intensified by |
| **B.** exacerbating | **E.** mask | **H.** unrelated to |
| **C.** replicating | **F.** restrain | **I.** used up in |
questions.stem:
*Official GRE Verbal Reasoning — TC Practice Set 2, original question 8*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

The reason minimum temperatures are going up more rapidly than maximums may involve cloud cover and evaporative cooling. Clouds tend to keep the days cooler by reflecting sunlight, and the nights warmer by (i) ________ loss of heat from Earth’s surface. Greater amounts of moisture in the soil from additional precipitation and cloudiness (ii) ________ the daytime temperature increases because part of the solar energy is (iii) ________ the evaporation of that moisture.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): A. inhibiting**
- **Blank (ii): F. restrain**
- **Blank (iii): I. used up in**
questions.explanation:
The second sentence asserts that clouds make for warmer nights by doing something to the loss of heat from Earth. Since less heat lost means more warmth, a word that means preventing or slowing heat loss is required for Blank (i). “Inhibiting” is therefore the answer. “Exacerbating” has the opposite meaning, while “replicating” makes no sense in this context. Since the first sentence asserts that daytime highs are increasing less rapidly than nighttime lows, Blank (ii) calls for a verb that indicates a moderation in rises in temperature during the day, and “restrain” has this sense. “Augment,” meaning to increase, has the opposite meaning, while “mask” would indicate that measurements are not reflecting actual increases in temperature, an idea not supported by the rest of the passage. The “because” in the last sentence indicates that the second clause explains how daytime temperature increases are restrained; it does so by making reference to solar energy and the evaporation of moisture. Because solar energy is responsible for increases in daytime temperature, the answer to Blank (iii) requires a word that explains how evaporation can lessen or divert that energy for other purposes. “Used up in” does this because it indicates that less solar energy is available to warm the Earth’s surface when a portion of it is instead devoted to evaporation. Neither “intensified by” nor “unrelated to” indicate a connection between solar energy and evaporation that would lessen warming.

Thus the correct answer is inhibiting (Choice A), restrain (Choice F), and used up in (Choice I).

*Explanation: [Official GRE Verbal Reasoning](gre_data/sources/verbal.pdf), PDF p. 87.*

questions.explanation:
The sentence defines normative ethics by specifying the sense of the “norms” for which it searches. Thus the correct answer is dictate (Choice D).

**Choose one answer.**

Researchers have observed chimpanzees feigning injury in order to influence other members of the group, thus showing that the capacity to ________ is not uniquely human.
questions.explanation:
The words “thus showing” suggest that the capacity that is not unique to humans was demonstrated by the activity the researchers observed. Since that activity—feigning injury to influence others—requires the capacity to transmit false information, “dissemble” is the correct answer. Because there is no indication that the chimpanzees worked together to feign injury, “conspire” is incorrect. None of the other options— “dominate,” “instruct,” or “cooperate”—suggests the pretense involved in feigning an injury, so they are all incorrect.

Thus the correct answer is dissemble (Choice D).

**Choose one option for each blank.**

The gaps in existing accounts of the playwright’s life are not (i) ________, since much of the documentary evidence on which historians have relied is (ii) ________.
questions.explanation:
The sentence focuses on the relationship between the gaps in existing accounts of a life and the evidence used to produce those accounts. Since “gaps” implies a concern with completeness, the characterization of that evidence that makes the most sense for Blank (ii) is “incomplete.” The other choices, “credible” or “extant,” could explain the accuracy or verifiability of the accounts in question but nothing about the gaps themselves. Once it is determined that “incomplete” is the best choice for characterizing the evidence, it follows that the gaps in the accounts based on that evidence would likely be considerable, so the opposite of considerable, “trifling,” is the correct answer for Blank (i).

Thus the correct answer is trifling (Choice A) and incomplete (Choice F).

*Explanation: [Official GRE Verbal Reasoning](gre_data/sources/verbal.pdf), PDF p. 90.*

*Official GRE Verbal Reasoning — TC Practice Set 3, original question 8*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

The serious study of popular culture by intellectuals is regularly credited with having rendered obsolete a once-dominant view that popular culture is inherently inferior to high art. Yet this alteration of attitudes may be somewhat (i) ________. Although it is now academically respectable to analyze popular culture, the fact that many intellectuals feel compelled to rationalize their own (ii) ________ action movies or mass-market fiction reveals, perhaps unwittingly, their continued (iii) ________ the old hierarchy of high and low culture.

| Blank (i) | Blank (ii) | Blank (iii) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A.** counterproductive | **D.** penchant for | **G.** aversion to |
| **B.** underappreciated | **E.** distaste for | **H.** investment in |
| **C.** overstated | **F.** indifference to | **I.** misunderstanding of |
questions.stem:
*Official GRE Verbal Reasoning — TC Practice Set 3, original question 8*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

The serious study of popular culture by intellectuals is regularly credited with having rendered obsolete a once-dominant view that popular culture is inherently inferior to high art. Yet this alteration of attitudes may be somewhat (i) ________. Although it is now academically respectable to analyze popular culture, the fact that many intellectuals feel compelled to rationalize their own (ii) ________ action movies or mass-market fiction reveals, perhaps unwittingly, their continued (iii) ________ the old hierarchy of high and low culture.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): C. overstated**
- **Blank (ii): D. penchant for**
- **Blank (iii): H. investment in**
questions.explanation:
The sentence discusses a purported change in how popular culture and high art are relatively valued; the author is scrutinizing the notion that the academic study of the former has significantly raised its once lowly status. In the last sentence, Blank (iii) is preceded by the word “continued,” indicating that something about intellectuals’ view of the hierarchy of culture has remained unchanged. Since the author states in the first sentence that this hierarchy was once dominant, “investment in” the hierarchy would indicate that sense of continuity. Neither of the other two options is supported by the passage because there is no indication the author believes that intellectuals have a long-held aversion to or misunderstanding of that hierarchy. The “although” that begins the last sentence indicates that the phrase completed by Blank (ii) will contrast the respectability of analyses of popular culture with something that nonetheless reveals a continued allegiance to the hierarchy. A need to explain away a “distaste for” or an “indifference to” action movies or pulp fiction would not indicate any such allegiance, so those choices must be incorrect. However, a need to justify one’s penchant or liking for popular culture would indicate an adherence to the high-low culture hierarchy. Thus “penchant for” is the correct choice for Blank (ii). Finally, since the author is suggesting that the hierarchy given to high and low culture is not obsolete as some claim, it follows that the shift in attitudes is exaggerated; thus, the correct answer to Blank (i) is “overstated.” “Underappreciated” implies the opposite, and “counterproductive” implies a judgment about the value of the hierarchy, whereas the passage is primarily concerned with its existence.

Thus the correct answer is overstated (Choice C), penchant for (Choice D), and investment in (Choice H).

*Explanation: [Official GRE Verbal Reasoning](gre_data/sources/verbal.pdf), PDF p. 91.*

questions.explanation:

Thus the correct answer is panacea (Choice C).

questions.stem:
*Official GRE Verbal Reasoning — Mixed Practice Set 2, original question 3*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

That the artist chose to remain in his hometown does not mean that he remained (i) ________; on the contrary, he (ii) ________ the international artistic movements of his day.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): A. provincial**
- **Blank (ii): F. kept abreast of**
questions.explanation:
The first part of the sentence suggests that the answer to Blank (i) names a quality that someone who chose to remain in his hometown might tend to have; in addition, the second part of the sentence suggests that this quality has to do with that person’s attitude toward the wider world. The answer choice for Blank (i) that best fits these conditions is “provincial,” so it is correct. Someone who is the opposite of provincial is interested in what is happening outside of his or her narrow domain, so the correct answer choice for Blank (ii) is “kept abreast of.” “Obstinate” may seem a plausible choice for Blank (i), as those who fit the “provincial” stereotype often not only are uninterested in other people’s opinions but also actively resist any pressure to change. However, “obstinate” by itself does not imply any particular attitude toward the world beyond one’s immediate environment, as one can be interested in other people’s opinions while at the same time clinging firmly to one’s own.

Thus the correct answer is provincial (Choice A) and kept abreast of (Choice F).

*Explanation: [Official GRE Verbal Reasoning](gre_data/sources/verbal.pdf), PDF pp. 150–151.*

*Official GRE Verbal Reasoning — Mixed Practice Set 2, original question 5*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

The lizards snapped up insects that are so (i) ________ that other potential predators avoid them. Among the lizards’ prey were some beetles that they initially (ii) ________ because the insects were spraying their hot, irritant defense chemical at the time. Yet even these produced no apparent ill effects, since the lizards, having eaten, proceeded on their way (iii) ________ enough.

| Blank (i) | Blank (ii) | Blank (iii) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A.** rare | **D.** sought | **G.** erratically |
| **B.** nutritious | **E.** rejected | **H.** laboriously |
| **C.** noxious | **F.** resembled | **I.** nonchalantly |
questions.stem:
*Official GRE Verbal Reasoning — Mixed Practice Set 2, original question 5*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

The lizards snapped up insects that are so (i) ________ that other potential predators avoid them. Among the lizards’ prey were some beetles that they initially (ii) ________ because the insects were spraying their hot, irritant defense chemical at the time. Yet even these produced no apparent ill effects, since the lizards, having eaten, proceeded on their way (iii) ________ enough.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): C. noxious**
- **Blank (ii): E. rejected**
- **Blank (iii): I. nonchalantly**
questions.explanation:
Blank (i) calls for a description of insects that predators would generally avoid. “Noxious,” meaning harmful, is the correct answer; there is no reason to suspect that predators would avoid nutritious or rare prey. Blank (ii) characterizes the lizards’ initial response to beetles they eventually ate, and since it is followed by a clause beginning with “because,” the lizards’ response must be explained by the beetles’ irritant-spraying behavior. “Rejected” fits these criteria; animals routinely avoid unpleasant stimuli. “Sought” is incorrect because it is unlikely that lizards would seek out prey with such defensive behavior, and “resembled” is incorrect because nothing else in the passage suggests that the described behavior is shared by the lizards. Finally, the author states that eating the beetles apparently did not harm the lizards; the “since” of the last sentence introduces the evidence on which this observation is based. Thus Blank (iii) must be filled by a word that suggests the lizards were unharmed. “Erratic” or “laborious” postmeal locomotion might indicate otherwise; therefore the correct answer for Blank (iii) is “nonchalantly.”

Thus the correct answer is noxious (Choice C), rejected (Choice E), and nonchalantly (Choice I).

*Explanation: [Official GRE Verbal Reasoning](gre_data/sources/verbal.pdf), PDF pp. 151–152.*

When the normally (i) ________ film director was interviewed, it was only the topic of her next movie that (ii) ________ her flow of words. Her (iii) ________ on that subject suggested that it was an unwelcome one.

| Blank (i) | Blank (ii) | Blank (iii) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **A.** assiduous | **D.** diverted | **G.** taciturnity |
| **B.** loquacious | **E.** stanched | **H.** alacrity |
| **C.** diffident | **F.** accentuated | **I.** rhapsody |
questions.stem:
*Official GRE Verbal Reasoning — Mixed Practice Set 2, original question 6*

**Choose one option for each blank.**

When the normally (i) ________ film director was interviewed, it was only the topic of her next movie that (ii) ________ her flow of words. Her (iii) ________ on that subject suggested that it was an unwelcome one.
questions.answerSource:
- **Blank (i): B. loquacious**
- **Blank (ii): E. stanched**
- **Blank (iii): G. taciturnity**
questions.explanation:
The reader is told that the director’s reaction to being asked about her next movie indicates that it is an unwelcome subject. Of the choices for Blank (iii), both “alacrity” and “rhapsody” would indicate excitement or eagerness to talk about this topic, making them implausible choices. “Taciturnity,” on the other hand, indicates an unwillingness or reserve about speaking; it is therefore the correct choice. This particular reaction is contrasted to the director’s normal conversational style, so the answer to Blank (i) must indicate a ready willingness to converse. “Loquacious,” meaning talkative, is the choice that fits; neither “diffident,” which means reserved, nor “assiduous,” which means diligent, conveys the necessary contrast to taciturnity. Finally, Blank (ii) suggests that the topic of the director’s next movie provoked a verbal reaction different from her usual one. Since the director is normally a talkative person, the unwelcome topic likely checked her conversation; therefore, “stanched” is the correct answer. “Accentuated” indicates the opposite, and while “diverted” might seem plausible, it suggests a potential change of topic unsupported by the rest of the passage.

Thus the correct answer is loquacious (Choice B), stanched (Choice E), and taciturnity (Choice G).

*Explanation: [Official GRE Verbal Reasoning](gre_data/sources/verbal.pdf), PDF pp. 152–153.*
